items.title: Lanny Morgan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999
items.q: When I was still on Maynard’s band, this was about 1961... I recorded it first with Maynard on “The New Sounds of Maynard Ferguson”

ctx.x: Yeah. Good to be a part of it. You came back, was it a conscious decision to come back and get into studio work on your part or did you just kind of fall into it?

Well I didn’t really, I didn’t have a thought of ever coming back to Los Angeles. But you know things had fallen to almost zero in New York. Maynard left in 1966 and I had a little group with Mike Abene and Ronnie McClure, Antonio Zalocco and a trumpet player named Dick Hurwitz, had a little quintet, and we made a demo, we had made a demo earlier, before the band broke up that I couldn’t sell, and I still have it, it’s a good demo, it really is. But I took it to Neshui Ertegun once on a cold winter’s night and he…
Wow. This was in New York?
